reports.title: TMC Provides Third Quarter 2026 Corporate Update

desk.headline: No revenue yet; loss narrowed to $28.4m ($0.06/share) vs $0.05 estimate; US permit decision step now due mid-December
results: TMC has no revenue yet. Its net loss shrank to $28.4m ($0.06 a share) from $184.5m ($0.46), when a $131m revaluation of a royalty liability hit results.
Exploration and evaluation spending rose to $23.5m from $9.6m on development, vessel and study costs; admin costs fell to $9.5m from $45.7m on lower share-based pay.
Cash was $79.3m with no financial debt; available liquidity was about $123m and the quarter used $19.4m of cash in operations.
US regulator NOAA moved its decision on certifying the USA-A commercial permit application to mid-December from end-October, to review over 1,600 public comments; its letter raised no deficiencies.
With Allseas, TMC is planning a lower-cost first production system; it may process first nodules at PAMCO's plant in Japan while two US agencies weigh funding for a Brownsville, Texas plant.

guidance.summary: No financial guidance. TMC still expects its US commercial permit before the targeted Q4 2027 start-up of its offshore collection system, says cash covers at least the next 12 months, and plans no other capital raising until government funding talks conclude.

watch: NOAA's certification decision on the USA-A application, expected by mid-December.
Outcome of the US government funding processes for onshore processing.
